problem: Energy-based models offer flexible distribution modeling but are hindered by unstable and inefficient training that limits their practical adoption.
approach: The method uses informative latent variables to guide joint energy learning while incorporating a cooperative generator for MCMC initialization, allowing optimization only in data space.
contribution: Demonstrates improved generation quality, training stability with fewer resources, and effective performance across multiple downstream tasks.

problem: Inference-time steering of diffusion models via composed experts fails when ratio-of-densities constructions create non-normalizable intermediate distributions despite valid endpoints.
approach: Provides a Path Existence Criterion to characterize well-defined composed densities and introduces Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE) supporting time-varying exponents via Feynman-Kac steering.
contribution: ACE prevents marginal path collapse, significantly outperforms constant-exponent baselines on drug design, and improves attribute success rates in compositional image generation.

problem: Autonomous vehicles struggle with the stability-plasticity trade-off: adapting to rare long-tail driving scenarios while preserving previously learned skills.
approach: NOMAD integrates non-parametric Bayesian memory with diffusion-based trajectory experts, mapping growing scene contexts to dynamic memory clusters that guide a conditional diffusion model functioning as a mixture of experts.
contribution: Achieves 9.4% improvement in interPlan score on nuPlan long-tail scenarios with positive backward transfer during continual learning.

problem: Existing estimators for score differences in diffusion models either lack statistical consistency or fail to scale in high dimensions, limiting transfer learning and discriminator guidance applications.
approach: Proposes a Sobolev-regularized estimator for score differences that ensures consistency and training stability, with convergence rate of Õ(n^(-(s-1)/(d+2s-2))).
contribution: Demonstrates improved stability in small-sample regimes and substantially outperforms non-regularized methods on transfer learning for ECG signal generation.

problem: Diffusion Transformers incur high computational costs due to dual forward passes in Classifier-Free Guidance and uniform calibration across transformer blocks regardless of varying sensitivity.
approach: RSTR jointly reduces temporal and spatial redundancy: Stage-1 uses evolutionary search to discover sparse guidance schedules with variable scales; Stage-2 applies adaptive rank allocation based on block sensitivity.
contribution: Achieves 50-70% compute savings while maintaining or improving quality, with 57% savings and 15% FID improvement on DiT-XL/2 and 3.43x speedup on Qwen-Image.

problem: Vision-language models struggle with multimodal entity tracking, exhibiting large performance gaps between text-based and image-based entity state tracking.
approach: MET-Bench evaluates VLMs on tracking entity states across three domains and modalities, revealing that performance gaps stem from visual reasoning deficits rather than perception limitations, with reinforcement learning applied to improve tracking.
contribution: Demonstrates that explicit text-based reasoning strategies improve performance but RL gains do not transfer robustly across input modalities, highlighting need for improved multimodal representations.

problem: Generative Flow Networks must train on offline datasets without access to active reward queries, but existing proxy-free methods impose coarse constraints limiting exploration effectiveness.
approach: TD-GFN uses inverse reinforcement learning to extract dense transition-level edge rewards from offline trajectories, guiding policy indirectly through DAG pruning and prioritized backward sampling to ensure robustness.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing baselines in convergence speed and sample quality for offline GFlowNet training.

problem: Bayes-assisted conformal prediction suffers when the Bayesian working model is misspecified, resulting in inefficient prediction sets despite preserving distribution-free frequentist coverage.
approach: RoBAS introduces robust nonconformity scores using heavy-tailed Bayesian models or empirical Bayes shrinkage, adapting to prior quality by exploiting reliable information while reverting to Distance-To-Average baseline when prior is weak.
contribution: Achieves competitive efficiency in absence of distribution shift while substantially reducing interval widths in shifted settings on tabular and image regression tasks.

problem: Generating human videos with realistic motions lacks decoupled control over foreground subject, background, trajectory, and action patterns, limiting flexible composition.
approach: RealisMotion uses a 3D world coordinate system for motion editing with trajectory control via unprojection and coordinate transformation, injecting subject as attention tokens while concatenating background and adding motion control signals.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on element-wise controllability and overall video quality with realistic decomposed motion control.

problem: In adaptive experiments, expensive labeled data collection is limited but large unlabeled datasets and pretrained models are available, yet leveraging predictions without validating inference is fundamentally challenging.
approach: PPAI integrates unlabeled data, predicted labels, and adaptively collected labeled data through a single estimating equation with adaptive weighting of predictions based on informativeness.
contribution: Enables valid confidence intervals and hypothesis tests with asymptotic variance no worse than labeled-only baseline and strictly smaller when predictions are informative.

problem: LLM-powered edge devices need cloud assistance for reasoning but static task routing based on difficulty overlooks subtask dependencies and misses parallelization opportunities.
approach: HybridFlow builds dependency-aware DAGs enabling concurrent subtask execution, with dynamic benefit-cost utility model optimizing trade-offs between accuracy, token cost, and latency in real-time.
contribution: Improves cost-accuracy trade-off while reducing latency and cloud API usage on GPQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME24, and LiveBench-Reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Schema linking for Text-to-SQL prioritizes textual similarity and inadvertently prunes topologically-critical bridge tables, severing relational pathways necessary for multi-hop joins.
approach: Graph-Link reformulates schema linking as constrained subgraph induction using hierarchical schema graphs and Steiner-tree optimization that guarantees topological connectivity while maximizing signal-to-noise ratio.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art schema linking with up to 7.0% improvement in recall/hit rates and 13.8% boost in SQL generation accuracy on complex queries on BIRD and Spider 2.0.

problem: Large-scale LLM training requires stable and efficient optimization, but existing orthogonal equivalence transformation methods incur high memory consumption and computational overhead.
approach: POET-X performs orthogonal equivalence transformations with significantly reduced computational cost while maintaining stability benefits of spectrum-preserving optimization.
contribution: Enables pretraining of billion-parameter LLMs on a single H100 GPU where standard optimizers like AdamW run out of memory.

problem: Long-form text generation from LLMs suffers from hallucination snowballing where early errors propagate and compound into subsequent outputs.
approach: SHARS uses an arbitrary hallucination detector to identify and reject hallucinated segments during generation, resampling until faithful content is produced while retaining only confident information.
contribution: Substantially reduces hallucinations in long-form generation while preserving or improving informativeness without requiring external resources like web search.

problem: Diffusion language models require fully-factorized output distributions because explicit joint modeling would produce prohibitively large parameter counts, creating a speed-coherence trade-off.
approach: CoDD replaces fully-factorized output distributions with a lightweight probabilistic inference layer that models complex joint dependencies while remaining compact.
contribution: Matches reasoning performance of computationally intensive RL baselines at a fraction of training cost and prevents collapse in few-step generation.

problem: Federated fine-tuning of LLMs faces severe statistical heterogeneity from intrinsic data distribution mismatches that model-level defenses typically overlook.
approach: FedSDR augments Federated Self-Distillation with a dual-stream mechanism: LoRA-S for smoothing to absorb heterogeneity via distilled data and LoRA-R for rectification anchored to raw data for factual correctness.
contribution: Yields a globally aligned and faithful model with superior performance compared to conventional algorithms.

problem: Simulation-based inference struggles with effective multimodal modeling as existing methods ignore structural disparities between parameters and observations via brute-force fusion strategies.
approach: FUSE employs a dual-track architecture preserving distinct features of multimodal inputs with FK-steered sampling leveraging intermediate observation likelihoods to guide generative trajectories.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on SBI benchmarks and successfully resolves complex parameter degeneracies in exoplanet orbital estimation.

problem: Analyzing attention weights as a standard interpretation approach neglects geometric properties of value vectors being aggregated, providing incomplete mechanistic insights.
approach: Contribution Weights measure token influence by accounting for attention weight, value magnitude, and directional alignment with layer output via projection-based metrics.
contribution: Provides more faithful measure of token importance than attention-based metrics and enables novel analysis revealing attention sinks suppress information through convex relationship with output norm.

problem: Optimizing training efficiency and model performance for data-driven weather forecasting requires understanding empirical scaling relationships across model size, dataset size, and compute budget.
approach: Analyzes scaling laws for weather models finding that data scaling shows stronger effects than parameter scaling and optimal allocation favors larger training datasets over increased model size.
contribution: Aurora exhibits strongest data-scaling (10x data→3.2x loss reduction) and reveals weather models favor increased width over depth, contrasting language model scaling behaviors.

problem: Fixed-vocabulary language integration for image clustering causes inter-modal semantic misalignment due to granularity discrepancy while overlooking intra-modal semantic redundancy.
approach: MAGIC prompts vision-language models to generate multi-granularity descriptions and designs modality-specific adapters that refine features into clustering-friendly representations under task guidance.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods through effective multi-modal alignment and reduced semantic redundancy.

problem: Extending neural optimal transport to high-dimensional Riemannian manifolds is challenged by curse of dimensionality: discrete approximations require exponentially more parameters with manifold dimension.
approach: Riemannian Neural OT (RNOT) uses continuous neural-network parameterizations incorporating geometric structure by construction while avoiding discretization.
contribution: Approximates Riemannian OT maps with sub-exponential complexity in dimension and demonstrates improved scalability relative to discretization-based baselines.

problem: Autoregressive decoding imposes fundamental latency bottleneck for real-time LLM function calling needed by embodied intelligence and interactive agents.
approach: RealtimeTool introduces special tokens compressing low-entropy tokens (4-6x reduction) while enabling independent parallel generation of function names and arguments.
contribution: Achieves 3-6x end-to-end speedup (up to 9.6x) with only 8.2% parallelization overhead and enables 16 Hz real-time control on consumer GPUs.

problem: Pixel-level accurate segmentation of structural cracks across diverse scenarios struggles with balancing crack topology modeling and computational efficiency.
approach: SCRWKV uses Structure-Field Encoder with Geometry-guided Bidirectional Structure Transformation to capture topological correlations and Dynamic Self-Calibrating Decay to suppress noise propagation.
contribution: Achieves F1 score of 0.8428 and mIoU of 0.8512 on TUT dataset with only 1.22M parameters, significantly outperforming SOTA methods.

problem: Dynamic graph anomaly detection with limited labeled anomalies faces gap between unsupervised methods producing ambiguous boundaries and semi-supervised methods overfitting to rare labeled data.
approach: Framework uses residual representation encoding capturing deviations from context, restriction loss constraining normal representations within co-centered hyperspheres, and bi-boundary optimization with normalizing flows.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority across diverse evaluation settings in learning discriminative and generalizable anomaly detectors.

problem: Text-to-image model evaluation predominantly focuses on image realism and shallow text-image alignment, lacking assessment of complex semantic understanding and world knowledge integration.
approach: WISE benchmark includes 1000 meticulously crafted prompts across 25 subdomains in cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning, and natural science with novel WiScore metric for knowledge-image alignment.
contribution: Reveals significant limitations in 20 models (10 dedicated T2I and 10 unified multimodal) regarding ability to effectively integrate and apply world knowledge.

problem: Point clouds from diverse domains with distinct sensing geometries, densities, and priors are typically handled separately, missing benefits of unified representation learning.
approach: Utonia trains a single self-supervised point transformer encoder jointly across five heterogeneous domains (remote sensing, outdoor LiDAR, indoor RGB-D, CAD models, video-lifted clouds).
contribution: Learns consistent representation space with improved perception, benefits embodied and multimodal reasoning, and demonstrates emergent behaviors from joint training.

problem: Efficient aggregation methods for quantile inference under privacy constraints with heterogeneous datasets remain underdeveloped.
approach: Framework constructs weighted estimators by adaptively aggregating quantile estimates from target and source sites under local differential privacy with adaptive weights minimizing asymptotic variance.
contribution: Establishes consistency, normality, and effectiveness with rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrates robust inference across heterogeneous scenarios.

problem: PPO's ratio clipping mechanism is structurally ill-suited for large vocabularies as it over-penalizes low-probability token updates while under-constraining high-probability shifts.
approach: DPPO substitutes heuristic clipping with principled constraint based on direct policy divergence estimates (Total Variation or KL) using efficient Binary and Top-K approximations.
contribution: Achieves superior stability and efficiency compared to PPO with more robust foundation for RL-based LLM fine-tuning.

problem: Existing relational deep learning methods neglect class imbalance problem in relational database entity classification, under-representing minority entities.
approach: Rel-MOSS designs relation-centric minority synthetic over-sampling with relation-wise gating controller to modulate neighborhood messages and relation-guided minority synthesizer.
contribution: Yields average improvement of up to 2.46% in Balanced Accuracy and 4.00% in G-Mean compared to SOTA RDL methods.

problem: Current evaluation methods for video generation models rely on subjective judgments or trajectory matching, lacking rigorous assessment of physical law adherence.
approach: Morpheus is physics-informed evaluation framework using 130 real-world videos capturing physical phenomena guided by conservation laws, assessing plausibility via interpretable metrics.
contribution: Reveals that contemporary models struggle to encode Newtonian physics despite generating aesthetically pleasing videos, identifying critical pathways for enhancement.

problem: Training CT-specific VAEs from scratch incurs substantial cost and degrades under heterogeneous scanners, protocols, and diseases.
approach: Foundation VAE leverages pretrained natural-image VAE for frozen encoder-decoder serving as unified interface for CT reconstruction, augmentation, and generation.
contribution: Achieves 3.9% NSD improvement for segmentation on reconstructions and 3.9% lower FVD with 36.2% higher CT CLIP score for generation.

problem: LLM long-context inference incurs significant memory overhead as KV cache scales linearly with sequence length and batch size.
approach: OBCache formulates cache eviction as layer-wise structured pruning using Optimal Brain Damage theory, quantifying token saliency via output perturbation with closed-form scores.
contribution: Improves long-context accuracy on LLaMA and Qwen models by replacing heuristic scores with output-aware signals.

problem: Chain-of-Thought reasoning lacks efficiency: models generate unnecessary tokens long after reaching correct answers, and early termination risks incorrect conclusions.
approach: Detects Confidence Region transitions via CUSUM change-point detection algorithm for real-time inference control, enabling early exit and test-time scaling.
contribution: Achieves 63.06% accuracy with 11.1% token reduction, outperforming DEER and Dynasor by 3.28% and 4.36% respectively.

problem: Model-induced label noise from Foundation Models and pre-trained experts introduces systematic errors tightly coupled with local feature manifolds, defying classical transition matrix approaches.
approach: MIND decouples noise into tractable subspace-dependent components via Latent Manifold Disentanglement, with Latent Decoding Estimator projecting samples into clusters with consistent error modes.
contribution: Significantly outperforms SOTA on controlled CIFAR-100 and structural stress tests on 3D datasets, effectively correcting Vision-Language Model zero-shot hallucinations.

problem: Unsupervised and supervised tensor network learning have developed in parallel, missing opportunities for cooperative advancement.
approach: MTNL unifies fields by fusing multiple TNs in deep-network style and develops flexible TN structure search with theoretical guarantees, combined within Bayesian framework.
contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness on tensor recovery, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and tensor regression with lightweight uncertainty quantification.

problem: Monolithic neural network simulators lack essential features of traditional numerical simulators: physical interpretability, reliability, and constraint satisfaction.
approach: Neural Modular Physics decomposes elastic dynamics into physically meaningful modules connected through intermediate physical quantities with specialized architecture.
contribution: Demonstrates superior generalization to unseen conditions, stable long-horizon simulation, better physical property preservation, and feasibility with unknown dynamics.

problem: Predicting Hamiltonian matrices for electronic structure calculations via SO(3)-equivariant networks requires costly Clebsch-Gordan tensor products, limiting scalability.
approach: QHNetV2 achieves global SO(3) equivariance via efficient SO(2)-equivariant operations on SO(2) local frames, eliminating costly tensor products.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on QH9 and MD17 datasets with strong generalization across molecular structures.

problem: NeRF latent spaces are implicit and globally entangled, making localized editing and physically grounded manipulation difficult while deformation sensitivity causes artifacts.
approach: Affine-Equivariant Kernel Space Encoding aggregates features via anisotropic Gaussian kernels enabling stable interpolation under transformations with feature distillation from hash grids.
contribution: Provides intuitive localized scene editing via Gaussian kernels without retraining while maintaining high-quality rendering.

problem: Graph neural networks for mixed-integer linear programming model locality limits representation power for combinatorial optimization.
approach: Proposes attention-driven neural backbone with element-centric view and dual attention performing parallel intra-type self-attention and inter-type cross-attention.
contribution: Consistently outperforms GNN-based architectures across instance, element, and solving-state level tasks.

problem: Reasoning LLMs generate extended chain-of-thought that is fragile to information loss during decoding, making KV cache compression challenging without disrupting reasoning.
approach: RLKV uses reinforcement learning to discover which attention heads maintain reasoning consistency, enabling aggressive compression on non-critical heads while retaining full cache on reasoning-critical heads.
contribution: Enables 20-60% cache reduction with near-lossless performance and up to 2.06x end-to-end speedup at 60% reduction across diverse tasks.
